banner.title: The DSG UNDERGROUND WATER TRAVEL, R518: printed pp. 46-48 (pdf 47-49) - the water travel opener (the deepening riverbeds lifting old access tunnels a dozen or more feet above the water, the low ceiling making boat travel impossible, the absent weather against the winding passages, the folding boat and the weaker collapsible boats and the creature boats of inhabited regions, and the scale cut-out model for tight bends), the Table 21 movement rates grid (the eight boat types from the small rowboat 90/120 through the large barge 20/30 to the small canoe and kayak at 120/180, subject to water flow, with maximum speed counting as hard work), the Table 22 standstill grid (1/3 rounds for the small rowboat up to 5/10 for the large barge), the movement-relative-to-water-only rule with the 60-ft stream and 90-ft canoe netting 30 upstream and 150 downstream, the Table 23 draught and ceilings grid (from the 1/2-ft small rowboat under a 2-ft ceiling to the 1-ft large barge under 4 ft), the Table 24 nonproficiency penalties (the -30/-15/-15/-10/-5/-60/-30/-60 movement modifiers and the 5/10/0/0/0/20/10/25 capsize chances), the one-proficient-stops-capsize and half-proficient-stops-penalty exemptions, the collision rules (the lantern and beacon and infravision, the vision-range rule, the d100 blind-travel check), the Table 25 collision probability grid (narrow 1-5-20/10-20-40, average 0-2-10/5-10-20, wide 0-0-4/1-4-8 proficient/nonproficient), the 5%-per-30-ft damage math with the 15% example and the difference-reading hull damage, the Table 26 boat damage grid (the eight percent bands from the 01-05 slight leak through the 45-60 hull split to the 99-00 no damage), the drop-off rules (5% per foot for damage and capsize, the 99/00 miraculous survival, the Proficiency Check save), the bailing rules (strenuous exercise, one character canceling one small hole), and the capsizing rules (the loose objects, the 1d4-round refloat, the float-downstream rescue, and the boatwright repair seam)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~5963-6300) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 63-65 = printed pp. 46-48) - every numeric cell dual-confirmed: the six tables reconstructed positionally from the Capture Tm coordinates where the djvu columns garble (Oar/Paddie, ftir, bargelraft, 1/28, 112ft, 114 ft, 113 ft, lft, 4%, dlOO, 4100 = d100, 2096 = 20%, 1096/1596 = 10%/15%). The Tables 21-24 share one boat key order (small rowboat, coracle, large rowboat, small barge/raft, large barge, small canoe, large canoe, kayak). The DMG page 54 movement seam and the DSG page 25 boatwright seam are noted. The Mining section (Where to Mine, p. 48) starts the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: Six tables pin in one round, the most since the cave-in arcs: Table 21 (8x2 speeds), Table 22 (8x2 standstill rounds), Table 23 (8x2 with the fractions pinned as whole units - draught in inches, ceiling in half-feet - so 1/3 ft pins as 4 inches and 1 1/2 ft as 3 half-feet), Table 24 (8x2 with the movement penalties as positive magnitudes, minus in the name and comment per the R514 convention), Table 25 (9 rows keyed width x 3 + flow, proficient and nonproficient percents), and Table 26 (8 lo/hi bands with 00 read as 100; the hull-split band pins as 45-60 exactly as printed, overlapping the 21-45 large-holes band at 45 - the R517 overlap lesson: pin as printed, never repair the book). Every effect die pins as dice + sides consts per the R508 convention (1d6 hours, 2d4+2 turns, 2d4, 1d6 rounds, 1d6 pieces, 1d4 refloat rounds). The DMG page 54 and DSG page 25 seams are noted; nothing auto-credits.

printed pp. 43-46 (pdf 44-47) - the standing water rules

50/100% flow, the 0-40 rate with the x20 ft/round, the six

1d6 with 6 = none / 1d4 ft, 3d6 / 1d8 ft), the damming
math (1000 cu ft per flow per turn, double wide / quarter
narrow, 1d6 worker points vs flow destruction,
50/150/250 completed CPVs per the DMG 109-110 seam, the
half-flow leak), the temperature ladder (1d4-mile warmth,
6d6 boiling no-save with -2/die min 1, 1d6 very hot,
bath-warm immunity), and the access rules. The djvu
garbles: 10096 = 100% flow, "flow rate - 2-6" = 2-6
(Capture settled), plus a stray STRUCTGRAL DECAY heading
interrupting the waterways opener in djvu (Capture

consts.name: dnuT21RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 21 boat movement rates grid carries eight boat types.

consts.name: dnuT22RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 22 standstill grid carries the same eight boat types.

consts.name: dnuT23RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 23 draught and ceilings grid carries the same eight boat types.

consts.name: dnuT24RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 24 nonproficiency grid carries the same eight boat types.

consts.name: dnuT25RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 25 collision probability grid carries nine cells: the three waterway widths against the placid, medium and rapid flow bands.

consts.name: dnuT26RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 26 boat damage grid carries eight percent-damage bands.

consts.name: dnuExampleStreamFtPerRound
consts.comment: the worked example: a stream flowing 60 feet per round.

consts.name: dnuExampleCanoeFtPerRound
consts.comment: a canoe traveling upstream at 90 feet per round in that stream.

consts.name: dnuExampleUpstreamNetFt
consts.comment: the upstream canoe is actually only moving 30 feet per round past the bank - boat movement is relative to the water only.

consts.name: dnuExampleDownstreamFt
consts.comment: the same canoe traveling downstream streaks along at 150 feet per round relative to the stream's bank.

consts.name: dnuDamageBasePctPerSlice
consts.comment: the base chance of suffering collision damage is 5% for each 30-feet-per-round slice of the boat's speed.

consts.name: dnuDamageSpeedSliceFt
consts.comment: the speed slice of the collision damage formula: 30 feet per round.

consts.name: dnuExampleDamagePct
consts.comment: the worked example: a boat traveling 90 feet per round has a damage probability of 15%.

consts.name: dnuExampleHullDamagePct
consts.comment: the worked example: a damage roll of 05 against the 15% probability is 10% less, so the boat's hull has suffered 10% damage - the hull damage is the difference between the die roll and the damage probability.

consts.name: dnuDropoffDamagePctPerFoot
consts.comment: a boat plunging over a drop-off checks for damage just as in a collision, but the chance is 5% per one foot of the drop-off, not based upon the boat's speed.

consts.name: dnuDropoffCapsizePctPerFoot
consts.comment: the chance of capsizing over a drop-off is also 5% per one foot of drop-off.

consts.name: dnuRefloatRoundsDice
consts.comment: it takes 1d4 rounds to refloat a capsized boat.

consts.name: dnuRefloatRoundsSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 1d4-round refloating roll, pinned as dice + sides consts per the R508 convention.

consts.name: dnuT26SlightLeakHoursDice
consts.comment: the 01-05 band: the boat leaks slightly and will founder after 1d6 hours.

consts.name: dnuT26SlightLeakHoursSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 1d6-hour slight-leak roll.

consts.name: dnuT26SmallHoleTurnsDice
consts.comment: the 06-10 band: water pours in from a small hole and the boat founders in 2d4 + 2 turns.

consts.name: dnuT26SmallHoleTurnsSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 2d4-turn small-hole roll.

consts.name: dnuT26SmallHoleBonusTurns
consts.comment: the +2 turns added to the small-hole 2d4 foundering roll.

consts.name: dnuT26ManyHolesDice
consts.comment: the 11-20 band: water pours in from 2d4 small holes and the boat founders in 2d4 turns - both rolls share the 2d4 shape.

consts.name: dnuT26ManyHolesSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 2d4 rolls for the many-holes band.

consts.name: dnuT26LargeHoleRoundsDice
consts.comment: the 21-45 band: large holes in the hull, the boat founders in 1d6 rounds.

consts.name: dnuT26LargeHoleRoundsSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 1d6-round large-hole roll.

consts.name: dnuT26PiecesDice
consts.comment: the 61-80 band: the boat breaks into 1d6 pieces.

consts.name: dnuT26PiecesSides
consts.comment: the sides of the 1d6-pieces roll.

bools.name: dnuRiverbedDeepeningRaisesTunnels
bools.comment: the torrents of rushing water gouge their channels, so riverbeds grow deeper and access tunnels that once fed into a river below its surface may now end a dozen or more feet above the water.

bools.name: dnuLowCeilingBlocksBoatTravel
bools.comment: the water might be deep enough for the heaviest of boats, but if the ceiling drops to within a few feet of the water, travel by boat is quite impossible.

bools.name: dnuWeatherAbsentUnderground
bools.comment: the dangers presented by weather are generally absent from the underground; low ceilings and tortuously winding passages create the replacement problems.

bools.name: dnuFoldingBoatIdeal
bools.comment: enchanted vessels such as the folding boat are ideal for dungeon adventuring, since they can easily be carried through narrow passages and down stairways.

bools.name: dnuCollapsibleBoatsWeaker
bools.comment: collapsible boats, while expensive and weaker than normal boats, provide another means of traversing underground waters.

bools.name: dnuCreatureBoatsAcquirable
bools.comment: in inhabited or heavily traveled regions characters might find boats used by underground creatures - borrowed, bought, or otherwise acquired.

bools.name: dnuScaleModelForTightBends
bools.comment: when carrying a boat into a dungeon the DM must note the boat dimensions against the passage sizes; in tight series of turns a scale cut-out model of the boat over a detailed corridor map shows whether it fits.

bools.name: dnuMovementRelativeToWaterOnly
bools.comment: boat movement is relative to the water only; the rate must be combined with (added to or subtracted from) the water movement to get the movement relative to land.

bools.name: dnuMaxSpeedIsHardWork
bools.comment: a character propelling a boat at maximum speed is considered to be working hard for purposes of the fatigue and exhaustion rules.

bools.name: dnuCoastingReverseOfAcceleration
bools.comment: the acceleration procedure applies in reverse to determine how long a boat continues coasting forward when its crew attempts to stop it.

bools.name: dnuRatesAssumeProficientCrew
bools.comment: the listed movement rates assume at least one character helping to propel the boat has boating proficiency.

bools.name: dnuMoveModifierEachRound
bools.comment: the nonproficiency movement modifier is applied to each round of operation at normal or maximum speed.

bools.name: dnuCapsizeOnEntryExitAndRisky
bools.comment: the capsize chance is rolled each time a character enters or leaves the boat and on any other occasions the DM feels are risky - turning around in a mild current, retrieving something from the water, standing up.

bools.name: dnuOneProficientStopsCapsize
bools.comment: if at least one person with boating proficiency is present in the boat, the capsize chance does not apply.

bools.name: dnuHalfProficientStopsPenalty
bools.comment: if at least half of the characters paddling or rowing have boating proficiency, the movement penalties do not apply.

bools.name: dnuPenaltiesAssumeMediumOrSlower
bools.comment: all of the nonproficiency penalties assume the boat moves through water of medium flow or slower; riding rapids or cascades is much more challenging.

bools.name: dnuLanternAvoidsDarkCollisions
bools.comment: a boat that carries a lantern or beacon can light the water before it sufficiently to avoid collisions due to darkness; if the light is snuffed or the progress is especially fast, the danger of smashing into a rock becomes very real.

bools.name: dnuVisionRuleAvoidsCollisions
bools.comment: obstacles can be avoided if the range of vision of the characters on board is greater than the distance the boat travels in one round.

bools.name: dnuInfravisionCanNavigate
bools.comment: infravision is sufficiently sensitive to the differences between the water and its bed to navigate a boat.

bools.name: dnuBlindTravelChecksEachRound
bools.comment: if vision does not extend far enough, the craft must check each round it travels blind, rolling d100 against the Table 25 collision percentage (the djvu garble 4100 = d100, settled by the Capture dlOO read).

bools.name: dnuDamageCheckIsD100
bools.comment: when a collision is indicated, roll d100 again and compare to the damage probability; a result equal to or less means the boat sustains damage.

bools.name: dnuHullDamageIsDifference
bools.comment: the exact extent of collision damage is the difference between the die roll and the damage probability, expressed as a percent of the boat's hull strength.

bools.name: dnuDropoffMiraculousSurvival
bools.comment: any time the drop-off damage roll is made and the result is 99 or 00, the boat miraculously survives the fall undamaged.

bools.name: dnuCapsizeProficiencyCheckPrevents
bools.comment: if a drop-off capsize is indicated but a character with boating proficiency is aboard, any one such character can attempt a Proficiency Check; success means the capsize was prevented.

bools.name: dnuBailingStrenuousUnlessSlight
bools.comment: characters not rowing or steering can bail water from a ruptured hull; bailing is strenuous exercise for the fatigue and exhaustion rules unless the boat is only leaking slightly.

bools.name: dnuBailingCancelsOneSmallHole
bools.comment: a single character can bail enough water to cancel the effects of one small hole in the hull, given a suitable container and all of his time devoted to bailing.

bools.name: dnuCapsizeDropsLooseObjects
bools.comment: a capsized boat tips over and fills with water; all loose objects fall free and must be recovered individually.

bools.name: dnuRecoveryImpossibleInRapidWater
bools.comment: in rapidly moving water, recovery of scattered items is usually impossible.

bools.name: dnuCapsizedBoatsDoNotSink
bools.comment: capsized boats do not sink, so characters unable to get their footing can hang onto the boat and float downstream until they can refloat it.

bools.name: dnuDamageRequiresRepairBeforeRefloat
bools.comment: if the boat was damaged when it capsized, the holes must be repaired before refloating (see the boatwright proficiency on DSG page 25).

tables.name: Table 21: BOAT MOVEMENT RATES
col_comments: the normal oar/paddle speed in feet per round, subject to the speed and direction of water flow: 0 small rowboat 90, 1 coracle 30, 2 large rowboat 45, 3 small barge/raft 30, 4 large barge 20, 5 small canoe 120, 6 large canoe 90, 7 kayak 120.
the maximum oar/paddle speed in feet per round: 0 small rowboat 120, 1 coracle 45, 2 large rowboat 60, 3 small barge/raft 45, 4 large barge 30, 5 small canoe 180, 6 large canoe 120, 7 kayak 180.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 21 boat movement rates grid (the djvu garble Oar/Paddie = Oar/Paddle)

tables.name: Table 22: MOVEMENT FROM A STANDSTILL POSITION
col_comments: rounds to reach normal speed from a standstill: 0 small rowboat 1, 1 coracle 1, 2 large rowboat 2, 3 small barge/raft 2, 4 large barge 5, 5 small canoe 1, 6 large canoe 1, 7 kayak 1.
rounds to reach maximum speed from a standstill: 0 small rowboat 3, 1 coracle 3, 2 large rowboat 5, 3 small barge/raft 6, 4 large barge 10, 5 small canoe 2, 6 large canoe 3, 7 kayak 2.

tables.name: Table 23: BOAT DRAUGHT AND CEILINGS
col_comments: the depth of water required below the surface, pinned in inches: 0 small rowboat 1/2 ft = 6, 1 coracle 1/2 ft = 6, 2 large rowboat 3/4 ft = 9, 3 small barge/raft 3/4 ft = 9, 4 large barge 1 ft = 12, 5 small canoe 1/4 ft = 3, 6 large canoe 1/3 ft = 4, 7 kayak 1/4 ft = 3.

the minimum ceiling needed to pass unimpeded, pinned in half-feet: 0 small rowboat 2 ft = 4, 1 coracle 3 ft = 6, 2 large rowboat 3 ft = 6, 3 small barge/raft 3 ft = 6, 4 large barge 4 ft = 8, 5 small canoe 1 1/2 ft = 3, 6 large canoe 2 ft = 4, 7 kayak 1 1/2 ft = 3.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 23 draught and ceilings grid (fractions pinned as whole units: draught in inches, ceiling in half-feet)

tables.name: Table 24: NONPROFICIENCY PENALTIES FOR BOAT USE
col_comments: the nonproficiency movement modifier pinned as a positive magnitude with the minus in this name and comment, applied each round at normal or maximum speed: 0 small rowboat -30, 1 coracle -15, 2 large rowboat -15, 3 small barge/raft -10, 4 large barge -5, 5 small canoe -60, 6 large canoe -30, 7 kayak -60.

the capsize chance percent, rolled on entering or leaving the boat and other risky occasions: 0 small rowboat 5%, 1 coracle 10%, 2 large rowboat 0, 3 small barge/raft 0, 4 large barge 0, 5 small canoe 20% (the djvu garble 2096 = 20%), 6 large canoe 10%, 7 kayak 25%.

tables.name: Table 25: COLLISION PROBABILITY
col_comments: the collision percent with boating proficiency (the number before the slash), rows 0-2 narrow / 3-5 average / 6-8 wide against placid, medium and rapid flow: narrow 1/5/20, average 0/2/10, wide 0/0/4.
the collision percent without boating proficiency (the number after the slash): narrow 10/20/40, average 5/10/20, wide 1/4/8.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 25 collision probability grid (row key = width x 3 + flow: 0 narrow placid through 8 wide rapid)

tables.name: Table 26: BOAT DAMAGE
col_comments: the low end of the percent-damage band: 0 leaks slightly at 01, 1 small hole at 06, 2 many holes at 11, 3 large holes at 21, 4 hull splits at 45, 5 breaks into 1d6 pieces at 61, 6 splinters at 81, 7 no damage at 99.
the high end of the percent-damage band with 00 read as 100: 05, 10, 20, 45, 60, 80, 98, 100.
